original_question: Determine for which permutations σ and π the order complex Δ(σ, π) associated with the interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset is shellable.
target_in_paper: Section 5.2, item 4 of the questions reproduced from [19, Question 31]: "For which σ and π is Δ(σ, π) shellable?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended open problem very closely: it uses the right interval [σ, π] in the permutation pattern poset, the right topological object Δ(σ, π), and the right property to classify, namely shellability.
missing_details: State explicitly that σ and π are finite permutations with σ ≤ π in the classical permutation pattern poset P ordered by pattern containment.
Define Δ(σ, π) precisely as the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), i.e. after removing the minimum element σ and maximum element π from [σ, π].
Clarify that shellability is the shellability of this abstract simplicial complex Δ(σ, π).
Make clear that the question is unrestricted in the paper: it asks for all pairs σ, π, not only layered, separable, decomposable, or unique-occurrence cases.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is part of this problem; those notions are inapplicable here and should not be imported into the statement.
refined_question: In the classical permutation pattern poset P of all finite permutations ordered by pattern containment, characterize the pairs of permutations σ ≤ π for which the order complex Δ(σ, π) := Δ((σ, π)) of the open interval (σ, π), obtained from the interval [σ, π] by deleting its endpoints, is shellable.
justification: Section 5.2 introduces the order complex for intervals in the permutation pattern poset, explains that for an interval [σ, π] one studies the order complex of the interior obtained by deleting the endpoints, and then reproduces four open questions from [19, Question 31]. The fourth of these is exactly the shellability-classification problem your draft is aiming at. The nearby context also explains why shellability is a natural strengthening of having the homotopy type of a wedge of spheres and gives a concrete non-shellable example, but it does not add extra hypotheses such as separability or layeredness. Therefore the closest paper-faithful refinement is the same broad question, made self-contained by spelling out the poset, the interval relation σ ≤ π, and the fact that Δ(σ, π) means the order complex of the open interval (σ, π), not of the closed interval [σ, π].

citations.label: definition of the order complex of an interval and the convention that Δ(σ, π) comes from the open interval obtained by deleting endpoints
discussion immediately after Question 31, including the example [321, 316254] where Δ is not shellable
